status: local evidence reconciliation in review; no actual acceptance

inheritedEvidence.kind: actual local catalog adverse/parity controls; separate from journal proofs

scenarios.trigger: Intent missing, malformed, unacknowledged or wrong target
scenarios.requiredOutcome: No dispatch; refuse or stop unavailable; no invented successful intent.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Strict model envelope/intent admission and simulated offline appends refuse; invalid process plans refuse before fork. The parent advances only after checking actual fixed bytes.
scenarios.remainingGap: No production durable intent backend or effect dispatcher is exercised. A parent file acknowledgement is not independent durable admission; absence of dispatch evidence cannot establish no prior effect.

scenarios.trigger: Crash after durable intent but before dispatch evidence
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Treat possible dispatch as unknown; fresh authoritative inventory, not automatic re-execution.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Intent-only reconstruction retains unknown and blocks blind/new-operation replay. A real killed child at count three restarts under the retained parent checkpoint and preserves unknown.
scenarios.remainingGap: The intent is synthetic, no SQL/provider action was possible, and the parent survives. Durable intent across parent/host loss and authoritative resource reconciliation remain unproved.

scenarios.trigger: SQL commit succeeds; outcome append fails or response is lost
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Quarantine; retain known commits, reconcile exact inventory; no rollback claim or password reset.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Simulated outcome-append outage preserves unknown. Partial outcome and complete-but-unacknowledged line five refuse in a fresh child; the parent stays at count four/unknown.
scenarios.remainingGap: No SQL commit or commit-response loss occurred in these journal proofs. The complete tail is a synthetic label, not an observed database commit; no automatic adoption, truncation or reconciliation follows.

scenarios.trigger: CREATE DATABASE or provider response times out
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Unknown effect; no blind retry, delete, adoption or assertion of provider idempotency.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Supplied response_lost/unknown and unavailable observation coexist; foreign/ambiguous observations refuse modeled retry.
scenarios.remainingGap: No CREATE DATABASE, provider timeout, supported idempotency key or request lookup was tested. Real response loss and resource provenance require separately authorized effect/provider evidence.

scenarios.trigger: Same name exists without established operation provenance
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Foreign or ambiguous resource preserved; quarantine; name/OID/hash alone cannot authorize cleanup.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Foreign/ambiguous/unavailable synthetic inventory blocks re-entry. An actual second file writer refuses an existing fixture journal without overwriting it.
scenarios.remainingGap: Existing-file refusal is not ownership-of-creation proof for an existing same-name role/DB/provider resource. Synthetic inventory and matching names/digests cannot authorize adoption or cleanup.

scenarios.trigger: App commits and CMS fails, or reverse
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Both unreleased; per-step commits retained; fresh paired inspection and reviewed forward re-entry only.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Modeled app success/CMS unknown stays separate; count five restarts with app success and CMS not_dispatched. Earlier real one-sided app/CMS migrations retain commits and refuse the pair in both directions.
scenarios.remainingGap: The real partial-commit tests are separate from both journal proofs. No integrated durable intent/outcome journal, lifecycle release admission, reviewed forward continuation or continuous worker fencing is established.

scenarios.trigger: Owner reversed but original grantor/ACL graph differs
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Remain incompatible; no inverse-command compensation or learning the defect as a new baseline.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: PR #49 records the preparation finding that reversing owner changes did not recreate an ACL graph; its final isolated owner-sink controls compare against the frozen baseline. Earlier object drift also refuses.
scenarios.remainingGap: The original grantor-collision finding is documented preparation evidence, not a newly executed or final-suite reproduction of that exact sequence. No compensating repair/provisioning journal exists.

scenarios.trigger: Two participants start from different project DBs on same cluster
scenarios.requiredOutcome: One common coordination domain; loser times out bounded before any role mutation; distinct per-DB keys insufficient.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: One memory model atomically blocks overlapping unresolved operations/stale heads. Existing participating pair batches contend on the actual app-DB transaction advisory lock.
scenarios.remainingGap: No shared lifecycle authority spanning participants originating from different app/CMS paths, all mutation/rotation/recovery paths or concurrent journal writers exists. The Node active flag is only one fixture-session admission.

scenarios.trigger: Per-DB migration lock busy after common coordination acquired
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Bounded stop, record no dispatched mutation or specific observed/unknown effects; close owned handles.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Earlier app migration-lock contention refuses and releases its lock; pair read-lock contention and killed read-only executor cleanup are separately observed.
scenarios.remainingGap: The common lifecycle allocation followed by a busy inner migration lock is not composed with journal intent/outcomes. Existing independent lock tests do not establish this ordering or no-mutation boundary.

scenarios.trigger: Coordinator session lost while another SQL session can still commit
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Stop new dispatch; quarantine and reconcile old in-flight work; new epoch cannot claim target fencing.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Modeled authority loss blocks appends until supplied quiescence/fresh review. Existing killed lock sessions refuse pair observations; actual read-only executor death releases its sessions/lock.
scenarios.remainingGap: No in-flight SQL effect on another session or accepted provider request is fenced/reconciled. Killing the owned Node child proves only that child termination, not absence or cancellation of remote work.

scenarios.trigger: Expired lease, stale epoch or restarted executor
scenarios.requiredOutcome: No timeout-only takeover, reusable receipt or inferred process termination; fresh admission/reconciliation required.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Modeled stale epoch/older operation and concurrent/cross-session child plans refuse. Fresh child reads use the exact retained parent checkpoint and reject exported receipt authority.
scenarios.remainingGap: No real lease/epoch authority, independent current checkpoint, parent-loss takeover or distributed atomic append is proved. PID/timeout/new epoch cannot supply old target-work quiescence.

scenarios.requiredOutcome: Invalidate observation; operating change paths and fresh inspection required; advisory lock cannot exclude it.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Earlier fresh both-DB reads and post-crash ACL/password faults invalidate prior handoff evidence; repaired state needs a fresh read/process.
scenarios.remainingGap: These are controlled faults around observations, not exclusion of an external administrator/control plane or uninterrupted coordination through handoff. Provider operating windows and external-change authority remain undecided.

scenarios.trigger: Restore requires source and separate target coordination
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Canonical multi-target order; source preserved; contention/identity mismatch refuses without effects.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Earlier actual archives restore into a separate local cluster, verify inventory and use fresh credentials; separate encrypted/signed privacy-journal custody retains quarantine during replay.
scenarios.remainingGap: No canonical ordered multi-cluster lifecycle coordination or contention/identity refusal is integrated with those restores. This child proof reads a temporary journal only; no source-loss/off-host acceptance follows.

scenarios.trigger: Observed rollback vs query failure with lost connection
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Only authoritative rollback proves no effect; unavailable observation and unknown effect may coexist.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: The model distinguishes unavailable observation from effect state and refuses unsupported success/no-effect combinations. Earlier real transactional migration failure rolls back DDL and history.
scenarios.remainingGap: Modeled no-effect is supplied evidence. The separate known-rollback test does not establish a journaled rollback under connection loss, uncertain commit response or surrounding provider/other-DB effects.

scenarios.trigger: Journal duplicate, reordered, truncated, forked or stale head
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Verify trusted checkpoint/current head; refuse inconsistent evidence; do not trust a self-consistent hash chain alone.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Wrong supplied heads/gaps/reorders/truncation refuse; fresh children refuse corrupt/tail files unchanged. A deliberate model control accepts a replacement chain with its own matching supplied checkpoint while authenticated remains false.
scenarios.remainingGap: The file reader compares an exact precompiled nine-record prefix and retained parent checkpoint. It is not a general journal importer or proof of authenticated/current independent checkpoint, anti-fork witness, durable CAS or parent-loss recovery.

scenarios.trigger: Journal or inspector unavailable after possible dispatch
scenarios.requiredOutcome: No new effects; best-effort sanitized local diagnostic is not durable success; preserve quarantine and uncertainty.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Modeled journal outage preserves uncertainty; fresh child missing/corrupt-file refusals preserve bytes/state. Earlier actual CMS permission loss yields unavailable and consumes old evidence.
scenarios.remainingGap: No dispatcher loses its durable journal/inspector after a real effect. Best-effort stderr or parent memory is not durable success, and separate SQL inspector failure is not integrated provisioning recovery.

scenarios.trigger: Exported receipt imported, fields unknown, sensitive text or generation changed
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Reject or redact by allowlist before persistence; receipt grants no authority; no bearer token/URI/password hash.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Exact allowlists/fixed diagnostics reject unknown/private fields and receipt imports; child events bind owned PID/run ID. Prior real password-change handoff failure remains separate.
scenarios.remainingGap: Opaque hex cannot establish whether a reference was derived from a secret. No production sanitizer/log-sink completeness, real secret-generation attestation, rotation/offboarding or trusted receipt import is established.

scenarios.trigger: All technical observations match but HS/S3/operator/provider approvals absent
scenarios.requiredOutcome: Evidence only; no runtime admission, APIs/frontends, provisioning, purchases or real notifications.
scenarios.reviewDisposition: evidence mapped; full proposed scenario remains open
scenarios.demonstratedEvidence: Completed synthetic steps yield technical evidence only; process evidence records false admission/hosted/product/trust flags and zero effects/notifications. Actual HS/S3 records remain null/empty.
scenarios.remainingGap: Local assertions and regression counts cannot appoint operators, accept funding/custody/provider capabilities, specialist/rights/privacy evidence or close actual S3 gates. Production runtime admission remains held.

nextProposal.purpose: Move beyond a single memory instance/Node active flag by observing bounded cooperative SQL locking and its limits without dispatching lifecycle mutations.
bounds: Disposable test support only; fixed read-only work queries and lock/session observations; no production executor, DDL/role/password/migration/repair/provider effect dispatch.

Use existing disposable fixture identities/targets and a fixed common fixture coordination endpoint; no production authority, maintenance DB, lock namespace, extra project role, role/membership policy exception or provider selection.
Compare actual common-endpoint contention from app/CMS work paths with an explicit separate-per-DB-lock control; report precisely which session/target is protected.
Bound common allocation and inner migration-lock contention without invoking a migration; no code-level mutation admission or lifecycle-wide serialization claim.

Observe owned coordinator-session loss while a separate fixed read-only SQL operation is in flight; test actual completion/refusal and cleanup without assuming a new epoch cancels old work. No target-fencing claim.
Test-first; preserve snapshots/roles/memberships, actual session/lock cleanup and held flags. Report safe-setup limits rather than broadening authority or weakening guards.
No independent journal durability/authentication, admitted re-entry/restore, provider capability, design-case or gate closure. All current holds and no provisioning/purchases/notifications remain.

limitations: Historical test counts overlap requirements; whole-suite CI counts rerun them and are not unique requirements or completion percentages.

PR #51 reconstructs a memory model; PR #52 restarts a Node child over a fixed temporary file while the parent keeps its simulated checkpoint. Neither is parent/host/DB/provider restart or independent durability/authentication/fencing.
File acknowledgement is verified byte agreement, not fsync/power-loss durability or current-head custody. The exact fixed-prefix reader is not a general journal importer.
Modeled inventory/quiescence/review/digests and dispatch/outcome labels do not establish real resource provenance, operator authority, SQL commit/rollback or provider effects.
Earlier real database/process/restore/custody evidence is credited separately; the privacy journal is distinct from the proposed provisioning journal.
Original design/scenario snapshots retain historical proposed fields unchanged. This additive view does not rewrite them as executed or accepted.
Required unchanged full regression may rerun existing disposable SQL/provider fixtures; that is not new implementation/scenario execution or an integrated provisioning proof.
